title: nf-core RNA-seq tutorial
text:
This tutorial walks through running an nf-core RNA-seq workflow in a reproducible way. It is designed for learners who are comfortable with the command line but new to Nextflow or nf-core.






Tip



The examples use nf-core/rnaseq, but the same structure applies to many nf-core pipelines.

5 Citation and credit
This tutorial uses community tools from nf-core and Nextflow. Update this page with the specific pipeline version, dataset, and citation details used in your workshop.

title: Setup
text:
Before running an nf-core pipeline, we need a place with enough temporary storage. On Unity, this is called a workspace. A workspace is a scratch directory that gives you more space for data, pipeline outputs, and temporary files.
Workspaces are temporary. The maximum duration is 30 days, but you can extend a workspace if you still need it. When you are finished, you can delete it.
More information: https://docs.unity.rc.umass.edu/documentation/managing-files/hpc-workspace/


Run:
ws_list
Example output:
(base) kfloer_smith_edu@login1:~$ ws_list
id: simple
     workspace directory  : /scratch3/workspace/kfloer_smith_edu-simple
     remaining time       : 11 days 7 hours
     creation time        : Wed May 20 18:42:17 2026
     expiration date      : Fri Jun 19 18:42:17 2026
     filesystem name      : workspace
     available extensions : 9998
In this example, I already have one workspace from a different project called simple.



Now create a new workspace called nf-core-demo that will last for 30 days.
Run:
ws_allocate nf-core-demo 30
Example output:
(base) kfloer_smith_edu@login1:~$ ws_allocate nf-core-demo 30
Info: could not read email from users config ~/.ws_user.conf.
Info: reminder email will be sent to local user account
Info: creating workspace.
/scratch4/workspace/kfloer_smith_edu-nf-core-demo
remaining extensions  : 10000
remaining time in days: 30
The important line is the workspace path:
/scratch4/workspace/kfloer_smith_edu-nf-core-demo
This is the directory we will use for the tutorial.



Run:
ws_list
Example output:
(base) kfloer_smith_edu@login1:~$ ws_list
id: nf-core-demo
     workspace directory  : /scratch4/workspace/kfloer_smith_edu-nf-core-demo
     remaining time       : 29 days 23 hours
     creation time        : Mon Jun  8 11:03:16 2026
     expiration date      : Wed Jul  8 11:03:16 2026
     filesystem name      : workspace
     available extensions : 10000

id: simple
     workspace directory  : /scratch3/workspace/kfloer_smith_edu-simple
     remaining time       : 11 days 7 hours
     creation time        : Wed May 20 18:42:17 2026
     expiration date      : Fri Jun 19 18:42:17 2026
     filesystem name      : workspace
     available extensions : 9998
Now I have two workspaces:

nf-core-demo, which we just created
simple, from an older project




Run:
cd /scratch4/workspace/kfloer_smith_edu-nf-core-demo
Your exact path may be different, so copy the path shown by your own ws_list output.



If your workspace is about to expire but you still need it, you can extend it.
Run:
ws_extend nf-core-demo 30
Example output:
(base) kfloer_smith_edu@login1:~$ ws_extend nf-core-demo 30
Info: extending workspace.
remaining extensions  : 9999
remaining time in days: 30
Check that the expiration date changed:
ws_list
Example output:
id: nf-core-demo
     workspace directory  : /scratch4/workspace/kfloer_smith_edu-nf-core-demo
     remaining time       : 29 days 23 hours
     expiration date      : Fri Aug  7 11:03:16 2026
Your exact expiration date will be different.



Only do this when you are completely finished with the tutorial files.
Run:
ws_release nf-core-demo
Then check your workspaces again:
ws_list
Example output:
(base) kfloer_smith_edu@login1:~$ ws_list
id: simple
     workspace directory  : /scratch3/workspace/kfloer_smith_edu-simple
     remaining time       : 11 days 7 hours
     creation time        : Wed May 20 18:42:17 2026
     expiration date      : Fri Jun 19 18:42:17 2026
     filesystem name      : workspace
     available extensions : 9998
Now nf-core-demo is gone, and only the older workspace remains.

title: Setup
text:
Check that Java is available:
java -version
Install Nextflow:
curl -s https://get.nextflow.io | bash
mkdir -p ~/bin
mv nextflow ~/bin/
Then check:
nextflow -version

title: Setup
text:
2 Choose a container engine
For local tutorials, Docker is often the easiest option:
docker --version
On HPC systems, Apptainer or Singularity is usually preferred:
apptainer --version

title: Setup
text:
3 Install nf-core tools
pip install nf-core
nf-core --version

title: Setup
text:
4 Create a project folder
mkdir nfcore-rnaseq-tutorial
cd nfcore-rnaseq-tutorial
mkdir data results work

title: Setup
text:
5 Prepare a samplesheet
Create samplesheet.csv:
sample,fastq_1,fastq_2,strandedness
sample1,data/sample1_R1.fastq.gz,data/sample1_R2.fastq.gz,auto
sample2,data/sample2_R1.fastq.gz,data/sample2_R2.fastq.gz,auto






Note



For a real tutorial, replace these paths with your actual FASTQ files or a small public test dataset.

title: Run the Pipeline
text: nextflow pull nf-core/rnaseq

title: Run the Pipeline
text: nextflow pull nf-core/rnaseq

title: Run the Pipeline
text:
2 Run a test profile
Start with the built-in test profile before using your own data:
nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq \
  -profile test,docker \
  --outdir results/test
If you use Apptainer:
nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq \
  -profile test,apptainer \
  --outdir results/test

title: Run the Pipeline
text:
3 Run your own samples
nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq \
  -profile docker \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir results/rnaseq \
  --genome GRCh38

title: Run the Pipeline
text:
4 Resume an interrupted run
nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq \
  -profile docker \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir results/rnaseq \
  --genome GRCh38 \
  -resume






Warning



Use the same command with -resume. Changing key parameters can invalidate cached work.

title: Run the Pipeline
text:
5 Record the exact command
Keep a copy of the final command in your notes or repository:
mkdir -p logs
nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq -profile docker --input samplesheet.csv --outdir results/rnaseq --genome GRCh38 2>&1 | tee logs/rnaseq.log

title: Interpret Results
text:
Open the MultiQC report:
open results/rnaseq/multiqc/star_salmon/multiqc_report.html
On Linux:
xdg-open results/rnaseq/multiqc/star_salmon/multiqc_report.html

title: Interpret Results
text:
Open the MultiQC report:
open results/rnaseq/multiqc/star_salmon/multiqc_report.html
On Linux:
xdg-open results/rnaseq/multiqc/star_salmon/multiqc_report.html

title: Interpret Results
text:
2 What to check first
Focus on:

Sequencing quality
Adapter content
Alignment rate
Duplication levels
Gene body coverage
Sample outliers

title: Interpret Results
text:
3 Common output folders







Folder
What it contains




fastqc/
Per-sample read quality reports


multiqc/
Aggregated quality-control report


star_salmon/
Alignment and transcript quantification outputs


pipeline_info/
Commands, software versions, reports, and provenance

title: Interpret Results
text:
4 Save provenance
Archive these files with your analysis:

pipeline_info/software_versions.yml
pipeline_info/execution_report.html
pipeline_info/execution_timeline.html
pipeline_info/params_*.json







Tip



The pipeline_info directory is one of the most useful places to look when you need to reproduce or debug a run later.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Check whether nextflow is on your PATH:
which nextflow
If it is missing, add the install location to your shell profile.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
Check whether nextflow is on your PATH:
which nextflow
If it is missing, add the install location to your shell profile.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
2 Docker is not running
Check Docker:
docker info
If this fails, open Docker Desktop or restart the Docker service.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
3 A run failed halfway through
Use -resume after fixing the problem:
nextflow run nf-core/rnaseq \
  -profile docker \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir results/rnaseq \
  --genome GRCh38 \
  -resume

title: Troubleshooting
text:
4 Disk space errors
Check the size of the work directory:
du -sh work results
Move large outputs to persistent storage before deleting anything.

title: Troubleshooting
text:
5 Where to look for help

The terminal error message
.nextflow.log
results/rnaseq/pipeline_info/
The nf-core pipeline documentation
The nf-core Slack community
